q: How do I calculate emissions from a refrigerated truck with a diesel refrigeration unit?
title: Emissions from a refrigerated truck
short: Add three parts: the truck engine's diesel x 2.68 kg CO2 per litre, the refrigeration unit's own diesel x 2.68, and any refrigerant topped up x its global warming potential. The refrigeration unit and refrigerant are what a dry-truck factor misses, so count them from fuel logs and service invoices.
audience: Cold chain operators and food, dairy and pharma shippers in India

sections.h: The three parts of a reefer truck's emissions
ul: Engine: litres of diesel for the trip x 2.68 kg CO2 per litre.
Transport refrigeration unit (TRU): if it has its own diesel engine and tank, its litres x 2.68. If you only have run hours, hours x the unit's litres per hour.
Refrigerant: kg topped up in the year x the gas's GWP, shared across the year's trips. This is CO2e because the gas is an HFC, not CO2.

sections.h: When the TRU has no separate fuel record
p: Some TRUs draw from the truck's main tank, and some log only engine hours. Use the manufacturer's fuel use per hour for your set point and ambient range, multiply by logged hours, and label it an estimate. Frozen loads at minus 18 degrees C in an Indian summer burn more than chilled loads at 2 to 8 degrees C, so do not use one rate for both. If the unit runs on shore power at the depot, that electricity is grid kWh x 0.710 (FY 2024-25 grid factor) kg CO2.

sections.h: Refrigerant GWPs for common reefer gases
ul: R-404A: about 3,943 (IPCC AR5) or 4,728 (AR6), worked out from its blend of R-125, R-143a and R-134a.
State which assessment report you used and keep it the same for the year.

p: If you own or lease and operate the truck, engine fuel, TRU fuel and refrigerant leakage are all your Scope 1. If you are the shipper and a transporter runs the truck, the whole trip is your Scope 3, Category 4 or Category 9 depending on who pays for the freight. Ask the transporter for litres and top-up records per trip; a tonne-km estimate for a dry truck will understate a reefer.

example.title: Worked example: one 600 km frozen-food trip
lines: Engine diesel: 150 L x 2.68 = 402 kg CO2
TRU: 20 hours x 1.5 L per hour (estimate) = 30 L; 30 x 2.68 = 80.4 kg CO2
Refrigerant: 3 kg of R-404A topped up in the year over 150 trips = 0.02 kg per trip; 0.02 x 4,728 (AR6) = 94.6 kg CO2e
example.note: Here the refrigeration unit and the refrigerant together add about 44 percent on top of the engine. A truck with a leak problem can add far more.

senseible: Senseible reads truck diesel invoices at 2.68 kg CO2 per litre and refrigerant top-up invoices, and its logistics calculator estimates freight by tonne-km and truck class. TRU run hours and per-trip refrigerant shares are figures you record alongside.
